standards_review.notes: git-workflow.md requires 'EPMCDME-####: Description'; review range includes 'checkpoint 2' (no ticket, no colon), 'docs: add spec for per-request require_confirmation flag' (no ticket prefix), and many 'feat(EPMCDME-13903): ...'/'fix(EPMCDME-13903): ...'/'refactor(EPMCDME-13903): ...' subjects that use conventional-commit type(scope) syntax instead of the documented format

code-quality.md Types And Imports requires 'X | None' unions/parameterized generics and 'from __future__ import annotations' in new modules; the new files src/codemie/agents/tool_confirmation/models.py, conversation_checkpoint_saver.py, src/codemie/service/tool_permissions_service.py and conversation_checkpoint_service.py all import and use typing.Optional[X] and omit the future-annotations import. License headers and first-party import alignment are otherwise satisfied across the changed tool_confirmation/service files checked

Sampled security-sensitive surface: CodeMieTool.is_safe defaults to False (fails closed) in src/codemie_tools/base/codemie_tool.py; _http_method_is_safe returns False on missing/unparseable method so github/gitlab/azure_devops_git/keycloak tool is_safe() overrides fail closed; resume_tool_call handler (assistant_handlers.py handle_tool_call_resume) checks Ability(user).can(Action.WRITE, conv) before resuming a conversation's pending tool call; ToolPermissionsService.get_effective_permissions applies the customer floor via ToolCallPolicy.stricter regardless of allow_override; the two new alembic migrations form a consistent, resolvable revision chain with matched down_revision. No credential logging or unsafe input handling found in the files opened
